Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022, as the township reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Ramsey County.
Minnesota townships govern the areas outside cities, mostly maintaining township roads; many contract with a city or fire district for fire protection.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
The township borrowed $6,550,000 during the year, which is not counted as revenue but helps explain spending above revenue.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: Minnesota local candidates file campaign finance reports with their city or township clerk, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
Cameras: no license-plate cameras are mapped inside White Bear Township's borders in OpenStreetMap as of 2026-10-20.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Minnesota yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
